Mixture of probabilistic PCA fitted to samples

Source: R/fit_mppca_samples.R
fit_mppca_samples.Rd

Fits a Gaussian mixture whose component covariances are restricted to \(\Sigma_k = W_k W_k^\top + \sigma_k^2 I\), where \(W_k\) has q columns (Tipping and Bishop, 1999). Each component varies mainly in a q-dimensional subspace, with equal noise variance in every other direction. With p variables a component has \(pq - q(q-1)/2 + 1\) covariance parameters instead of \(p(p+1)/2\), so the model can be fitted when a component holds fewer points than there are variables, where a full-covariance fit (fit_em_samples()) is singular.

Usage

fit_mppca_samples(
  target,
  N = 2L,
  q = 1L,
  n_starts = 5L,
  max_iter = 500L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  seed = NULL,
  canonicalise = TRUE
)

Arguments

target

A gmm_target carrying an n by p samples matrix.

N

Number of mixture components.

q

Dimension of each component's principal subspace, an integer with 1 <= q < p. Compare values of q (and N) with the BIC in the diagnostics.

n_starts

Number of k-means starts. The fit with the largest final log-likelihood is returned.

max_iter

Maximum number of EM iterations per start.

tol

Relative log-likelihood convergence tolerance.

seed

Optional integer seed for the k-means starts.

canonicalise

Logical. If TRUE (the default), components are sorted by gmm_canonicalise().

Value

A gmm_fit with regime = "sample". The diagnostics carry the log-likelihood trace and final value, the number of free parameters, BIC and AIC. metadata$mppca holds q, the loading matrices loadings and the noise variances noise_var, in component order.

Details

The fit is by EM. Given the responsibilities, the update of \((W_k, \sigma_k^2)\) is the closed-form maximum-likelihood solution of probabilistic PCA on the responsibility-weighted covariance \(S_k\): the columns of \(W_k\) are the leading q eigenvectors of \(S_k\), scaled by \((\lambda_j - \sigma_k^2)^{1/2}\), and \(\sigma_k^2\) is the mean of the remaining \(p - q\) eigenvalues. Starts are k-means partitions.

The result is an ordinary gmm_fit, so every operator of the package (conditioning, marginals, imputation, sampling) applies to it.

References

Tipping, M. E. and Bishop, C. M. (1999). Mixtures of probabilistic principal component analyzers. Neural Computation, 11(2), 443-482. doi:10.1162/089976699300016728

See also

Other fitting: fit_em_samples(), fit_kld_em(), fit_moment_match(), from_cf(), from_cf_elliptical(), from_cf_sources(), from_kde(), from_objective(), select_N()

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- 10
w1 <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(rnorm(p * 2), p)))
w2 <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(rnorm(p * 2), p)))
x <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(60 * 2), 60) %*% t(3 * w1) + matrix(rnorm(60 * p, sd = 0.3), 60),
           matrix(rnorm(60 * 2), 60) %*% t(3 * w2) + matrix(rnorm(60 * p, sd = 0.3), 60) + 4)
fit <- fit_mppca_samples(gmm_target_from_samples(x), N = 2L, q = 2L, seed = 1L)
fit@metadata$mppca$noise_var
#> [1] 0.08906958 0.09604513
fit@diagnostics$bic
#> [1] 2100.344
